quandoUsar: Showing the daily return of a portfolio, fund, or strategy over several months, with each month's total next to its name.
When the pattern matters more than the curve: streaks of good or bad days, the best and worst day, how many days closed up.
As a trading-day picker to drill down elsewhere on the screen, with `onSelectDate`.
quandoEvitar: Use `activity-heatmap` for unsigned daily counts, such as contributions or visits over a year.
Use `calendar` or `date-picker` when the user needs to pick any date; here only days with data are clickable.
Use `line-chart` when what matters is the cumulative evolution, not each day in isolation.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next day with data, crossing months, and show that day's tooltip.
Step back or forward five days with data (seven with `weekends`), which equals one week when there are no holidays in the way.
Go to the first or last day of the period.
Select the focused day; press again to clear the selection.
Enters the calendar on a single day (the last focused or the most recent) and leaves it.

acessibilidade: The whole is a `role="group"` named by `label`; each month is a `<section>` with month and total in its name, and each day with data is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`.
Focus uses a roving tabindex: only one day is in the `Tab` order and the arrow keys lead to the others; days without data are decorative and outside navigation.
Each day's name carries the full date and the return (`up`, `down`, or `flat` plus the percentage); these terms and the visible labels, such as `Best day` and `Closed`, are hardcoded in English.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the months rise one after another and each month's cells appear in a diagonal wave, growing from half size; the grand total counts up from zero to the value.
The tooltip is a single one: it appears already in place and then glides on a spring from one day to the next; with a mouse, the day under the cursor grows slightly.
With “reduced motion” on, months and cells only fade, the total appears directly, and the tooltip doesn't glide.
responsivo: Months are distributed into columns of at least 128 px according to the container's width; below 420 px they always sit in two columns.
On touch, the tooltip stays visible for about two seconds after the finger leaves, to give time to read.
desempenho: Each day with data is a `<button>` (a year of trading days gives about 250), and the wave entrance uses only CSS transitions with delay, with no JavaScript per cell.
notasIA: Pass `returns` as `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }`, with `value` in percentage points (`1.2` = +1.2%); days without an entry appear as closed and months without an entry aren't drawn.
Totals are compounded by default: `compound={false}` sums the returns, `weekends` shows Saturday and Sunday, and `scale` fixes the percentage at which the color saturates.

Controlled selection with `selectedDate` and `onSelectDate` (`null` = none) or internal with `defaultSelectedDate`; keep `returns` in `useMemo`, since the whole calendar is recomputed when the array changes.
